contract_plain_english: The passage describes finite volume methods for conservation laws: divide the domain into cells, approximate the integral of the conserved density in each cell or its cell average, and modify those values each time step using fluxes through cell edges. A cell average is the cell integral divided by cell volume. Numerical flux functions use the available approximate cell averages to approximate the correct fluxes; finding good such functions is the central numerical problem. [Raw PDF p.27, printed p.5, Section 1.2, first paragraph.] The inherited exact balance states that the time derivative of the integral between any two endpoints equals the physical flux at the first endpoint minus that at the second. Additional source terms are required when the quantity is not conserved. [Raw PDF p.26, printed p.4, equation (1.10) and following explanation.] Integral conservation remains the governing formulation at discontinuities, where the differential equation need not hold classically. [Raw PDF pp.26–27, Section 1.1.2.] This passage gives a qualitative method description, leaving the discrete update formula, numerical-flux stencil, and quantitative approximation properties unspecified.
